This is a minimal restatement of #4486. Both loop levels carry [unroll] and
every bound is a compile-time constant: j runs 0..2 and k runs 0..(3-j-1), so
the whole nest is six comparisons.

What to look for, per pane:

- SPIR-V panes (-spirv): scroll to the fragment entry point. Two structured
  loop headers survive, each with a back-edge and a phi for its counter, and
  only ONE float comparison inside them -- so the nest was not unrolled. Fully
  unrolled code would have no loop header and six comparisons.
- DXIL pane (no -spirv): the same source has no loop at all; the comparisons
  are materialised in straight-line code. Same shader, same attributes, two
  different answers.

Note CE builds Release binaries and appends its own debug-info flags to DXC
panes, so the embedded source you can see in the output is CE's doing, not the
shader's.
